newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian punters to buy state bookmaker.
newsitem.headline: Australian punters to buy state bookmaker.

text.p: Australia's most populous state New South Wales on Tuesday announced it would give punters the chance to buy a slice of the state-owned bookmaker by floating its Totalisator Agency Board (TAB).
The NSW government is cashing in on one of Australia's most popular pastimes, gambling, and is expected to raise between A$600 million (US$465 million) to A$1.0 billion from the sale.
"If caucus (government assembly) approves the proposal, during the next few months, the government will prepare the TAB for sale by public float," NSW state premier Bob Carr said.
TAB will become Australia's second state betting agency monopoly to float and join a growing number of gaming related companies to list on the local stock exchange in recent years.
The Victorian state government sold Tabcorp Holdings Ltd in a A$810 million float in 1994. The Queensland state government is currently looking into selling its betting agency business.

But analysts said the TAB sale is unlikely to be as good a bet as Tabcorp, citing the fact that the TAB was predominately involved in the horse racing industry, while Tabcorp also had a licence to operate slot-machines.

The NSW government's TAB float plans may also upset Australia's biggest gambler, and richest man, Kerry Packer, who was touted as a possible buyer of the TAB. Packer's gaming interests include the management of the Sydney casino.
NSW Treasurer Michael Egan said the government would limit individual shareholding in the TAB to five percent.

"By limiting each shareholding to five percent of the new TAB -- not just for the float, but thereafter -- we can ensure no one person or organisation controls the business and that ownership is spread through the community," Egan said.
